contentBlocks.body: for...of, spread ([...x]), Array.from and array destructuring all work with any iterable, not just arrays. An object is iterable if it has a [Symbol.iterator] method that returns an iterator: an object with a next() method returning { value, done }.
Strings, Maps, Sets and arrays are all built-in iterables. Plain objects are not: iterate them with Object.keys, Object.values or Object.entries instead.
`for (const x of { a: 1 })` throws TypeError: object is not iterable. Use `for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(obj))`.

payload.explanation: A Set is iterable and holds unique values, so spreading it yields each value once.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Which one is NOT iterable with for...of?

payload.explanation: Plain objects have no Symbol.iterator. Use Object.entries(obj) to loop over them.

payload.text: An iterator's next() method returns an object with a value and a ____ flag.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Make range(start, end, step) a real iterable by implementing its iterator's next() method.
